newsitem.title: USA: Mozambique could be HPIC debt relief candidate-IMF.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique could be HPIC debt relief candidate-IMF.

text.p: Mozambique could be a candidate for the new international initiative to ease the debt burden of poor countries adopting tough economic policies, a senior IMF official said on Sunday.
Jack Boorman, director of the International Monetary Fund's policy development and review department, told a news conference Mozambique had made good progress on economic reforms.
"Mozambique is a country which is deserving of assistance under the initiative and I would be pretty confident that it would receive it," he said.
Under the initiative for Highly Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC), creditors including Paris Club of creditor states agree to cooperate to ease an individual country's debt burden.
But Boorman said things could be slightly more complicated for Mozambique, where most of the debts are to Moscow and are denominated in now obsolete convertible roubles.
"Russia, a non-Paris Club bilateral creditor, is involved," he said.

Moscow, which inherited responsibility for the debts and the assets of the former Soviet Union, has rescheduled Soviet debts and is seeking membership of the Paris Club as a creditor state to help it get back some of the loans it extended to one-time allies in the developing world.
The debt deal, launched six months ago by the World Bank and IMF, aims to reward poor countries that are carrying out tough economic reforms by providing them with debt relief.
Up to 25 countries, most in Africa, are expected to benefit from the plan, which could cost creditors as much as $7.7 billion.
